h: Making the Most of Your Ice Time
p: An hour or two on the ice goes quicker than you'd think, so it pays to arrive a little early. Give yourself time to park, find the skate hire counter and get everyone's boots sorted before your session starts. There's nothing worse than watching the clock tick while you wrestle with a set of stubborn laces, so keep that buffer in mind.

Dress for the occasion, but don't overdo it. Layers are the way to go: a T-shirt, a jumper and a light jacket you can take off once you warm up. Gloves are essential, both for warmth and for when you put your hand down on the ice. Jeans are fine, though they get soggy if you take a few tumbles, so something quick-drying is even better.
If you've got younger children with you, a skating aid can be a game-changer. It gives them something to push and lean on, and it frees up your hands so you're not bent double the whole session.

North Bristol has more on offer once the skates come off. The Mall at Cribbs Causeway is right there for shopping and food, and the Blaise Castle Estate in Henbury is a cracking spot for a walk, with woodland paths, a big play area and its folly castle perched on the hill. Head into the city and you've got the Clifton Suspension Bridge, the harbourside and plenty more, making it easy to turn a skate into a full Bristol day out.
